name: Bingles' Blastencapper
summary: Bingles Blastenheimer’s explosive lies in trogg hands after his gyrocopter fell into the Loch. Its loss threatens his plans to aid Gnomeregan’s liberation.

sections.title: A Volatile Invention
sections.body: Bingles Blastenheimer’s Blastencapper was aboard his gyrocopter when it crashed in Loch Modan. The pilot built the explosive for aerial strikes against the troggs and leper gnomes who overran Gnomeregan. Mechanical failure sent his craft into the Loch, though Bingles survived. Troggs from the lake’s northern islands raided the wreckage and carried the volatile weapon back to their camps.

sections.title: Air Support for Gnomeregan
sections.body: Bingles needs the Blastencapper for the coming effort to retake Gnomeregan. The exiled gnomes are preparing to reclaim their radioactive home, and he counts on his gyrocopter and signature munitions for the air assault. The troggs of Loch Modan could accidentally trigger a catastrophe with the explosive, and its recovery would preserve a valuable weapon for the gnomish resistance.

faq.answer: Bingles Blastenheimer made the Blastencapper for aerial strikes against the troggs and leper gnomes occupying Gnomeregan.

faq.q: How did the Blastencapper end up in the Loch?
aliases: why is it in the loch
faq.answer: Bingles crashed his gyrocopter into the Loch. Troggs from nearby islands raided the wreckage and carried off his tools, including the explosive.
Troggs from the Loch’s northern islands took the Blastencapper from the wreckage and guard it in their camp.

faq.q: Why does Bingles need the Blastencapper returned?
faq.answer: Bingles needs the Blastencapper and his tools to repair his gyrocopter and launch an aerial assault in support of Gnomeregan’s reclamation.

angles.text: Every tool and munition matters as the gnomes struggle to reclaim Gnomeregan. Recovering Bingles’ explosive could let gnomish aerial ingenuity strike back at the trogg invaders.
The Blastencapper shows gnomish engineering flair: it is complex, explosive, and devastating when released from high altitude.
